title: SLO Adoption Micro-Experiments and Signal Harvesting Plan
content:
Purpose and framing:

This working doc lays out a lightweight, cross-functional experiment program to accelerate practical SLO adoption across product teams by running small, time-boxed micro-experiments that (1) test SLO definitions and alerting thresholds in production-like traffic, (2) harvest signal (what telemetry is actually useful), and (3) capture human operational costs of the new SLOs. Goal is to produce repeatable templates and concrete artifacts (dashboards, runbooks, alert filters, retro notes) teams can reuse when they opt to adopt SLOs at scale.

Why micro-experiments?
- Low barrier: short (2–4 week) focused work that reduces full-team disruption.
- Learn fast: iterate on signals, thresholds, and on-call ergonomics before committing to org-wide SLO policy.
- Cross-functional by design: requires eng, product, observability, and support input so the SLOs reflect user-facing priorities.

High-level success metrics for the program (what we’ll measure across experiments):
- Signal quality: fraction of alerts that are actionable within 30 minutes (target > 60% by experiment end)
- Threshold stability: number of threshold changes after initial rollout (target <= 2 changes in 8 weeks)
- Operational cost: Mean time spent per week by on-call to triage SLO alerts (target: document baseline and reduce over experiments)
- Adoption readiness: number of teams that sign an adoption checklist at experiment close (target: 3 pilot teams in Q2)

Cohort selection and scope:
- Candidate teams (pilot): Console routing, Hosted API ingestion, and Dedicated autoscaler. These map to distinct traffic/latency/cost profiles.
- Per-cohort SLO focus: availability (high level), p50/p95 latency for the primary RPC, and a correctness/quality heuristic (e.g., rate of malformed outputs or rerank accuracy) where applicable.
- Experiment limit: 1 SLO type per cohort per micro-experiment (so experiments stay narrow).

Experiment template (2–4 week cadence):
1) Week 0 — Setup (3–4 days):
   - Kickoff w/ product, eng, observability, and support (30–60m).
   - Define user journeys and key endpoints the SLO maps to. Short doc: 1-pager SLO hypothesis.
   - Instrumentation checklist: ensure metrics, traces, and example logs exist and are parsable. Tag required metrics with team and endpoint id.
   - Baseline run: collect 2 weeks of historical data where possible.

2) Week 1 — Shadow/Backtest (5 days):
   - Run SLO as "shadow" (no alerts) in prometheus/metrics pipeline and evaluate: burn rate distribution, peak contributors, false-positive signals.
   - Create draft dashboard: burn-rate, error budget, top contributing endpoints, per-region breakdown.
   - Initial retro at end of week with raw observations.

3) Week 2 — Canary alerting (5 days):
   - Enable low-noise alerting rules (notification only to a pilot channel or single on-call). Use throttle and noise filters.
   - Triage process: document steps for acknowledging, diagnosing, and resolving. Record time spent on triage for each alert.
   - Update dashboard with alert flow metrics.

4) Week 3–4 — Iterate and stabilize (5–10 days):
   - Tweak thresholds/filters based on real signals.
   - Try an automated remediation play if one exists (circuit-breaker toggle, fallback model, degraded mode). Measure time to remediate and user impact reduction.
   - Final retro and artifacts: adoption checklist, runbook draft, final dashboard, and playbook entry.

Roles & responsibilities (cross-functional):
- Eng SRE lead (owner): run experiment, manage instrumentation tasks, and coordinate dashboards.
- Product/PM: define user journey & acceptability criteria, help set initial threshold hypothesis.
- Observability (platform): assist with metrics ingestion, dashboard templates, and alert-suppression utilities.
- Support / CS: provide real-user incident context and expected business impact windows.
- Solutions Eng / SE: for Dedicated teams, ensure scaling signals map to customer-visible throughput metrics.

Instrumentation checklist (minimum):
- Metric for success/failure at request granularity (labelled by route/service).
- Latency histograms (p50,p95,p99) per route.
- Traces that capture the end-to-end user path and correlate with request ids.
- A lightweight synthetic probe for critical endpoints (5-min cadence).
- Error classification tags (e.g., client_error, model_failure, infra_error).
- A linkable dashboard template cloneable per team.

Signal harvesting guidelines (what to capture beyond basic metrics):
- Full alert payloads (at least sampled) to review root causes offline.
- Human annotation: a quick field on alerts where the responder marks whether alert was actionable and root cause category.
- Incident fatigue indicator: consecutive alerts within 24h for the same endpoint.
- Cost signal: approximate compute/token/egress deltas during incidents for the Hosted API cohort.

Measurement & analysis plan:
- Use a standard spreadsheet to collect: alert timestamp, alert type, on-call primary, time-to-ack, time-to-resolve, root cause tag, user impact estimate, follow-up action.
- Weekly digest: short summary of top 3 signals and one suggested change to threshold or filters.
- Post-experiment writeup: 1 page with evidence for final recommendation (adopt / iterate / reject). Attach dashboards and runbooks.

Communication & gating:
- Internal: weekly 30m sync with pilot stakeholders. Post experiments, present findings to Reliability Council.
- External (customers): for Dedicated cohort, coordinate customer comms templates if any planned remediation could be visible.
- Gating decision at experiment close: adoption checklist must be signed (observability, runbook, threshold rationale, rollback plan).

Risk log & mitigations (short):
- Risk: noisy alerts cause on-call burnout. Mitigation: start with low-sensitivity rules + suppression windows, require human confirmation before page escalation.
- Risk: missing telemetry for edge cases. Mitigation: synthetic probes and selective trace sampling; expand instrumentation before enabling alerts.
- Risk: business teams disagree on user impact thresholds. Mitigation: align on concrete user journeys and KPIs up-front; run a split-test for conservative/lenient thresholds.

Templates to produce (deliverables):
- 1-page SLO hypothesis doc (template provided).
- Dashboard clone URL (team-specific).
- Runbook draft with play-by-play triage steps and common RCA links.
- Post-experiment 1-page recommendation + adoption checklist.
- Experiment retro note (what surprised us, follow-ups).

Next steps (near-term):
- Week of Feb 16: kickoff pilots with Console routing and Hosted API ingestion (Aisha, Ben to run).
- Instrumentation owners assigned by Feb 18.
- Shadow run starting Feb 22, canary alerting Feb 29.
- Capture templates in GitHub repo and link to Confluence page CONFLUENCE-RELIABILITY-1482.

Open questions (for review):
- What burn-rate window should be standard for short experiments (5m, 15m, 1h)? Proposal: 15m for latency, 1h for availability.
- Do we require synthetic probes for every SLO pilot or only high-risk endpoints? Proposal: require probes for customer-facing write paths.

Notes to reviewers: informal doc, expect edits. We want to land on a small repeatable pattern (2–4 weeks) and a set of artifacts teams can consume. Please add comments inline or propose pilot teams if you think other services are a better first testbed.
